expansive

/ik-SPAN-siv/ - the stress falls on SPAN · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Expansive means spread out over a wide area or ranging across a wide scope — broad, open, and still opening outward.

From the fire tower the view is expansive — four counties, two rivers, and on clear mornings the faint smudge of the city.

Example

The new survey course is expansive by design: it opens with cave paintings and closes with video art, crossing thirty centuries and five continents in a single semester. Students complained they could never predict the next lecture; the professor took it as a compliment.

Expansive is the right word because the course keeps spreading outward — across eras, across continents, across forms. The word suits anything built wide and still opening: a lawn, a harbor view, a mind that ranges.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

sweeping: covering a great span in one motion — a sweeping view, a sweeping claim — and, applied to statements, it often hints the reach went too far to be careful. Expansive is roomy without the warning label.

wide-ranging: touching many different areas, strictly a matter of scope — a wide-ranging interview, wide-ranging interests. Expansive covers that same breadth and can also describe physical space itself: a terrace or a plain can be expansive, but not wide-ranging.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

cramped: squeezed into too little room

narrow: confined to a small range or focus

Where it sits · how far the spread keeps opening

broad → expansive → boundless

broad vs. expansive: Broad is weaker than expansive: broad states a generous width and stops there, while expansive adds openness — the sense that the spread keeps going past where you expected it to end.

boundless vs. expansive: Boundless is stronger than expansive: an expansive lawn still ends at a fence line somewhere, but boundless claims no limit exists at all.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — ex-: out (Latin)

Root — pans-: spread, stretched (Latin pandere)

Suffix — -ive: tending to

Put it together: Ex- (out) + pans- (spread — from Latin pandere, 'to spread, stretch') + -ive (tending to) = 'tending to spread out.' Whatever is expansive is built wide and behaves as if still widening — a view, a plain, a curiosity.

Use the root in a new word: expanse: Sailors learn to read moods in the expanse — a darkening to the west, a ripple line running east.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral / descriptive — travel writing, reviews, profiles

Expansive works two rooms: physical space (an expansive deck, an expansive plain) and scope (expansive interests, an expansive study). Applied to a person or mood, it means warmly open and talkative — over dinner he grew expansive. Do not let the eye swap it for expensive: different root, different claim, and the SAT enjoys the difference.
